text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A Riga court started considering a suit by the Latvian Social Democratic Party against Prime Minister Andris Shkele. The party says Shkele insulted it during a TV address a few days before the March local elections by accusing them of being Communist and posing a threat to Latvia.
- President Guntis Ulmanis, on a state visit in Poland, signed a bilateral free trade agreement. He discussed integration with both the EU and NATO.
- Latvia's hockey team lost 4:5 to Italy, seen as a serious defeat.
- The Constitutional Court started considering its first case, deciding on cabinet rules regulating business interests in the energy sector by 35 MPs.
- A new Latvian gas-carrier Kurzene has being built at the shipyard of Ulsan, Korea, and will be launched today. In mid-July its sister ship, Vidzeme, will also be launched.

- The question of recognising Latvia's aliens passports by Russia will be discussed at consular talks between the two countries next month in St.Petersbourg. The passports are handed to people without citizenship, mainly Russian-speakers.
- A fishing boat sunk in the early morning of April 27 while going through Swedish waters after being hit by a larger vessel. The crew of the boat was rescued.
- The budget had a 8.17 million lats surplus on April 22.
- One tonnes of diesel spilt from a Cyprus-registered tanker, Oivri, which was being filled at Ventspils port.
- The cabinet committee decided to have the state owned-stock of Lattelekom handed over to the privatisation agency.
- The EU is to participate in the funding of communications reconstruction projects in Latvia.
- The Latvian gambling business association argues that amendments to gambling laws will result in a loss of 1.5 million lats and deprive the state and local budgets of 392.000 lats.
